checks.name: JSON validity, schema, and required fields
checks.notes: Parses as UTF-8 JSON with 2-space indentation, double quotes, no trailing commas, and a final newline. Top-level keys, organ fields, lesson fields, and quiz fields match CONTENT_SPEC v1. Optional latin, alsoKnownAs, keyPoint, and heroStat fields are correctly typed. No markdown, HTML, emoji, bullet characters, double spaces, or trailing whitespace occur inside strings.

checks.name: Organ inventory, order, and uniqueness
checks.notes: Exactly the seven required IDs appear in spec order: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, retina, cochlea, vestibular-system. Every organ systemId is sensory. No ID duplicates an organ in another system: the 12 files contain 95 unique organ IDs.

checks.name: Lengths and field counts
checks.notes: System summary is 225 words in 3 paragraphs. Organ summaries are 157-170 words in exactly 2 paragraphs; taglines are 52-68 characters. Every organ has 3-5 functions with 15-23 word details, exactly 3 facts, 3 conditions, 2 sources, 3-4 relatedOrgans, 3-6 lowercase keywords, and a heroStat within the 12/24 character limits. The system has 3 stats and 5 functions, the longest function 67 characters.

checks.name: Medical accuracy spot-check
checks.notes: Spot-checked 12 claims against authoritative sources. Cochlea: 2.5 turns, ~9 mm base, ~5 mm height, and high-to-low pitch mapping (Britannica, https://www.britannica.com/science/ear/Cochlea; NIDCD, https://www.nidcd.nih.gov/health/how-do-we-hear). Hair cells: ~16,000 total, ~3,500 inner plus ~12,000 outer (Harvard BioNumbers; NIDCD hair-cell glossary). Cornea supplies about two thirds of focusing power (University of Utah Health; NEI). Humans carry ~400 functional odor receptor genes versus ~1,000 in mice (PubMed 16607462, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16607462/). Retina is ~1,094 square mm and 0.1-0.5 mm thick (Webvision, https://webvision.med.utah.edu/book/part-xiii-facts-and-figures-concerning-the-human-retina/). The tongue has ~10,000 taste buds (MedlinePlus Tasting, https://medlineplus.gov/ency/anatomyvideos/000148.htm) and eight paired muscles (TeachMeAnatomy, https://teachmeanatomy.info/head/muscles/tongue/). Ossicles boost pressure about 20 times (NIDCD; Stanford CCRMA), and threshold eardrum motion is below a hydrogen atom diameter (physiology teaching source). Bony semicircular canals are under 1 mm wide, otoconia are calcium carbonate, and cochlear hair cells do not regenerate in humans (Britannica; Cleveland Clinic, https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/vestibular-system).

checks.name: Source URLs and allowlist
checks.notes: All 14 unique source URLs were checked with curl -L on 2026-10-21 and returned HTTP 200. All hosts are on the allowlist: MedlinePlus, NEI and NIDCD (NIH), Cleveland Clinic, Kenhub, and TeachMeAnatomy. No Wikipedia, blog, or AI-generated URLs are present.

checks.name: Lesson structure and organ focus
checks.notes: Lesson id is lesson-sensory with exactly 8 steps, 8 minutes, and beginner level. Step 1 is the hook, step 8 is the recap and next steps. Steps 2-7 each carry a different organId: eyes, retina, ears, cochlea, vestibular-system, nose. Bodies are 105-114 words. Step 7 was corrected from tongue to nose so its organId matches its smell-and-flavor content; the tongue is still taught in that step and tested in the quiz.

checks.name: Quiz quality and answer distribution
checks.notes: Exactly 8 questions with ids sensory-q1 through sensory-q8, four unique options each, and a valid answerIndex. Correct indexes are 1, 1, 0, 3, 2, 0, 2, 1, so all four positions are used. Difficulty is 3 easy, 3 medium, and 2 hard. Explanations are 25-32 words and teach the reasoning. No all-of-the-above or none-of-the-above options, and every answer is supported by the file's own content.

checks.name: Safety and voice
checks.notes: No dosage, treatment, diagnosis, or symptom-management instructions. All conditions are descriptive and educational. Removed the clichéd windows-to-the-world label, reduced repeated which-is-why constructions from 10 to 0, and removed repeated pea and sheet-of-paper comparisons. No markdown, emoji, or bullet characters remain.

checks.name: Cross-system relatedOrganIds
checks.notes: All 22 relatedOrgans references resolve to existing organ IDs across the 12 system files, including mouth and salivary-glands (digestive), lungs (respiratory), and brain, cerebellum, brainstem, and hypothalamus (nervous). Counts per organ are 3-4, within the 2-4 limit.

changes: Corrected cochlear hair-cell division of labor: about 3,500 inner cells do most of the sensing and about 12,000 outer cells amplify, instead of saying all 16,000 do the hearing.
Corrected cochlear dimensions to a 9 mm base and 5 mm height, and changed the uncoiled length from 35 mm to the ~32 mm average.
Fixed lesson step 7 organId from tongue to nose so the stop matches its smell-and-flavor content.
Removed the claim that rods handle motion; rods are now described as dim-light and gray-scale sensors.
Corrected the retinal image comparison by removing held at arm's length, and changed the retinal thickness comparison from paper to a credit card.
Corrected the vestibular canal width from 0.3 mm to less than a millimeter and replaced the repeated pea comparison with a pencil eraser.
Corrected the tongue muscle count to eight pairs and changed most papillae carry taste buds to several kinds of papillae carry taste buds.
Changed the mouse olfactory receptor gene count from ~1,100 to ~1,000 and made the olfactory epithelium smaller than a postage stamp.
Changed glaucoma wording to say raised pressure can damage the optic nerve, and changed the two Meniere's descriptions to fluid buildup and fluid balance rather than vague pressure.
Fixed the post-spin vertigo description from the room tilting to the room keeps turning, and corrected vestibular crystal wording to press on hair cells.
Removed 10 instances of which is why, the windows-to-the-world cliché, and repeated paper and pea comparisons; varied the piano analogy and clarified compression and rarefaction.

Corrected about a million ganglion fibers to more than a million, the eardrum comparison to about as thin as paper, and the taste-bud distribution to ~10,000 on the tongue plus more on the palate and throat.
Corrected the Latin labels for Eyes and Ears to the plural Oculi and Aures.
Clarified that the cochlea reports sound rather than pitch alone, and that the auditory nerve carries its pattern to the brainstem.
remainingConcerns: Population averages such as 16,000 cochlear hair cells, 10,000 taste buds, and 120 million rods vary between individuals and are stated as approximations.
The lesson has six tour slots for seven organs, so the tongue has no dedicated step; it is taught inside the smell-and-flavor step and has its own organ entry and quiz coverage.
